title: Damage compensation needing a "verification payment" vs. replacement through the app
summary: The recipient received a damaged appliance from ShopKart and uploaded photos in the app. A caller from "ShopKart support" phones about the complaint and mentions both a replacement and a goodwill compensation amount. In the legitimate case, the agent schedules a replacement pickup through the app and adds the goodwill credit to the recipient's ShopKart balance; nothing is paid. In the fraud case, the caller says the compensation goes to the bank account only after the recipient sends a small "verification payment" to a UPI ID to "link" the account. The catalog originally used "card number and OTP" as the fraud mechanism; it was changed to a small outgoing "verification" payment so that this family does not duplicate `ec_09` and `ec_14`. Both cases mention compensation, bank or balance credit, and the word "verify".

shared_setting.recipient_profile: a ShopKart customer; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Product: a mixer grinder, kettle, or small speaker worth [AMOUNT_14] (₹1,500–₹12,000), delivered with a cracked body.
Goodwill compensation offered in both cases: [AMOUNT_16] (₹200–₹1,000).
The recipient really raised a damage complaint [TICKET_ID] with photos.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller requires the recipient to send money to a UPI ID in order to receive compensation. Receiving a payment never requires the receiver to pay first; the "verification" is the first step of a theft that usually escalates.
fraud.caller_objective: Get a first small transfer, then larger "verification" or "reversal" payments.
stable_facts: The caller says it will be "returned with the compensation within minutes".
The caller says the replacement will be "processed after verification".

markers.text: Replacement scheduled through the ShopKart app
Compensation credited to ShopKart balance by the company
Verification" refers to photos already uploaded, not a payment

cooperative.fraud: Says they are sending the small amount

clarifying.fraud: Asks why they must pay to receive compensation
clarifying.legitimate: Asks whether they must pack the item in the original box

resistant.fraud: Says the compensation can be sent without any verification or not at all
resistant.legitimate: Says they want a refund instead of a replacement

suspicious.fraud: Says sending money to get money is a known trick
suspicious.legitimate: Asks how they can check the call is from ShopKart

fraud: recipient sends the amount (cooperative only), after which the caller says it "failed" and asks for a larger amount
legitimate: agent converts the request to a refund to the original payment method
agent points the recipient to the complaint status in the app when suspicious.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may claim the first transfer failed and ask for a repeat or larger "verification"; this is the same mechanism. They must not switch to card details, OTPs, QR codes, or app installation. The legitimate agent must not request any payment, card detail, or code.

must_preserve: compensation offer and the word "verify/verification" in both cases
outgoing transfer to a UPI ID in _F
company-side credit and app-scheduled replacement in _L

ambiguities: Some real companies verify a bank account by sending a tiny amount to the customer. That direction is legitimate and is not used in this family, to keep the contrast on who pays whom.
A small amount is not safe because it is small; it is the evidence because of its direction.
Knowing the complaint details is not a cue; both callers know them.

evidence_references.claim: Refund scams ask victims to approve small "verification" transactions (CE22)
Fraudsters start with small fees and then ask for more (CE09)
A major marketplace states it will never ask for payment via phone (CE14)
